title: Oven-Roasted Korean Mackerel Jjigae
description: Fresh, crisp, crowd-pleaser Korean dish featuring mackerel, ice-bath-shock, ayurvedic-rajasic-friendly, served in a traditional Korean dosirak, cooked in a wok.
instructions: Season the mackerel fillets with salt and black pepper.
Heat the sesame oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add the mackerel fillets to the wok and sear for 2-3 minutes per side.
Transfer the mackerel to a baking sheet and roast for 8-10 minutes or until cooked through.
In a small bowl, whisk together gochujang, soy sauce, Korean chili flakes, brown sugar, garlic, and rice vinegar.
Add the sauce to the wok and stir to combine.
Add the green onions, sesame seeds, and a pinch of salt to the wok and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes.
Remove the mackerel from the oven and let it cool slightly.
Shock the mackerel in an ice bath to stop the cooking process.
Once the mackerel is cool, slice it into thin pieces and add it to the wok.
Stir-fry the mackerel with the sauce and garnish with scallions, sliced daikon, and cucumber.
Serve the mackerel jjigae in a traditional Korean dosirak with a side of steamed rice and Korean chili sauce.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve immediately.
